name: Regency Centers Corporation
executive_summary: Regency Centers Corporation (REG) is a grocery-anchored open-air shopping centre REIT whose portfolio quality and leasing momentum support the quantitative screen’s buy rating. The screen flags cash-flow cheapness (FCF yield 5.2%), dividend appeal (3.9% yield, dividend growth), and GARP (PEGY 0.06), offset by rich headline multiples (P/E 25.8, P/B 2.1) and elevated leverage. Primary filings show accelerating revenue and NOI through FY2025 and H1 2026, with covenant compliance intact; the central debate is whether operating strength and cash generation justify a premium to deep-value benchmarks, or whether geographic concentration, development spend, and a higher-rate backdrop cap upside.
investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen rates REG as buy (6/22 models, composite 65%, five families passed: cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk). That profile fits a quality-income value case rather than a net-net or Graham defensive one.

Business quality aligns with what the screen rewards. REG owns and manages 392 consolidated shopping centres plus partial interests in a further 90 properties (Q2 2026 10-Q), focused on neighbourhood and community centres anchored by grocers—tenants with relatively defensive traffic. No single tenant exceeds 10% of aggregate annualised base rent. Piotroski F-Score 7/9 confirms improving profitability, positive operating cash flow, and asset-turnover trends, though leverage is not declining and share count has not been fully flat.

The screen’s cheapness signal is cash-flow-led, not earnings-yield-led. FCF yield of 5.2% (screen TTM ~$743m) and operating cash flow of ~$828m (Yahoo FY2025; filing H1 2026 OCF $434m) compare favourably to a 3.9% earnings yield that fails several earnings-multiple screens. Dividend growth is tangible: the common dividend rose to $0.755 per quarter in 2026 from $0.705 in 2025 (Q2 2026 10-Q), supporting the High Dividend Yield and Dividend Growth model passes.

Growth is visible in primary filings. Shopping-centre NOI rose to $1,123m in FY2025 from $1,047m in FY2024 (+7.3%), and H1 2026 NOI reached $597m versus $554m in H1 2025 (+7.6%). Net income attributable to common shareholders for H1 2026 was $237m ($1.30 diluted EPS) versus $209m ($1.15) in H1 2025. News coverage (see below) cites record leased occupancy and raised 2026 guidance; those operating KPIs are not fully recoverable from the truncated filing body extracts.

What the screen does not capture—and why this remains a selective, not blanket, buy—is structural leverage (debt/equity ~72%, net debt ~$4.6bn per Yahoo FY2025), geographic concentration (California 24.7%, Florida 19.9%, New York City metro 12.8% of ABR per Q2 2026 10-Q), and ongoing development/acquisition capital deployment (~$212m in H1 2026 on developments and improvements, plus ~$96m gross acquisitions). For a value investor, REG offers cash-flow-backed income and operational compounding at a fair-to-full earnings multiple, not a margin-of-safety deep-value entry.

**Annual results (10-K, FY ended 31 December 2025 and 31 December 2024)**

Filing body extracts for both 10-Ks are present but truncated; segment footnotes nonetheless provide consistent annual figures.

FY2025 revenue grew 6.9% and NOI 7.3% year on year. Net income rose 32%, aided by higher equity-income from partnerships and lower impairment versus prior periods. Real estate at cost reached $14.56bn at 31 December 2025 (from $13.70bn at end-2024), reflecting $614m acquired properties and $383m developments/improvements.

Balance sheet and liquidity (10-K FY2025): total debt ~$4.74bn (notes payable $4.62bn plus $120m on the $1.50bn unsecured revolver). Management reported compliance with all unsecured debt and revolver covenants as of 31 December 2025. Revolver availability was ~$1.4bn after borrowings and letters of credit. Environmental remediation accrual: $19.2m.

**Yahoo fallback (used only where filings lack a figure)**

FY2025 free cash flow / operating cash flow of $827.7m and net debt of $4.63bn are taken from `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo), as the 10-K body extracts do not include a full cash-flow statement. These align directionally with H1 2026 filing OCF of $434m.

**Data gaps**

Filing body extracts are truncated at ~80,000 characters; MD&A sections containing NAREIT FFO, same-property NOI growth, and physical occupancy percentages are largely absent from the archived bodies. Operational KPIs cited in the news section below cannot be verified from primary filing extracts in this pack and should be treated as unconfirmed until the full 10-Q MD&A or earnings supplement is reviewed.
risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical and tenant demand.** Filings explicitly warn that trade policy, inflation, consumer confidence, and recession risk could impair tenant profitability, occupancy, and rent growth (Q2 2026 10-Q, Item 1 notes). Grocery-anchored open-air retail is relatively defensive but not immune.

**Geographic concentration.** California (24.7%), Florida (19.9%), and the New York City statistical area (12.8%) each exceed 10% of ABR (Q2 2026 10-Q). Weather, regulation, and local economic shocks are amplified.

**Leverage and refinancing.** Total debt ~$4.9bn against equity of ~$7.1bn at 30 June 2026. The screen fails Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Financial Health, and Schloss models on leverage and liquidity (current ratio 0.80). Scheduled 2026–2027 maturities include $166m (remainder of 2026) and $758m in 2027 (Q2 2026 10-Q debt maturity table). Management states covenant compliance; no going-concern language appears in available extracts.

**Development and acquisition risk.** H1 2026 capital deployed to developments ($212m) and acquisitions ($96m gross) exceeds disposition proceeds ($14m). News flags development and financing-cost risk. Q2 2025 included a $1.3m real-estate impairment on a property subsequently sold.

**Environmental and legal.** Environmental accrual of $16.4m (30 June 2026) and $19.2m (31 December 2025). Filings state ordinary-course litigation is not expected to be material; no defaults on senior securities reported.

**Governance / capital structure.** $225m of Series A/B preferred stock (6.25% / 5.875%) ranks ahead of common. ATM programme ($500m authorised, none issued H1 2026) and new $500m repurchase authorisation (no repurchases H1 2026) provide flexibility but also potential dilution if equity is issued into weakness.

**Preferred equity and REIT accounting.** Reported ROE (8.2%) and P/E (25.8) understate economic leverage inherent in the REIT structure; FFO-based analysis is standard for the sector but unavailable in filing extracts here.

RiskTags: cyclical, leverage, competitive, other
news_highlights:
Coverage in `news_manifest.json` is thin and heavily clustered around the Q2 2026 earnings cycle (late July–mid August 2026); limited material news beyond that window is captured.

- **“Regency Raises 2026 Outlook as Leasing Momentum Builds Into Year-End”** (12 August 2026) — management raised full-year guidance on occupancy, leasing, and NOI; signed leases and rent spreads cited as growth drivers.
- **“REG's Q2 FFO Beat Estimates on Leasing Momentum, '26 View Raised”** (30 July 2026) — Q2 FFO above consensus; outlook raised on rent and occupancy gains and stronger tenant recoveries.
- **“Regency Centers (REG) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Record Occupancy and Raised ...”** (30 July 2026) — 3.8% same-property NOI growth cited; development pipeline noted.
- **“Regency Centers (REG) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript”** (8 August 2026) — core operating earnings of $1.16 per share cited.
- **“Is Regency Worth Buying as Leasing Strength Meets Development Risk?”** (12 August 2026) — balanced view: leasing strength versus higher financing costs and market concentration.
- **“Regency Centers (REG) Stock Looks Cheap On Cash Flow But Fair On Earnings”** (3 August 2026) — DCF-oriented commentary suggesting cash-flow-based discount versus earnings-based fair value.
- **“Are Wall Street Analysts Bullish on Regency Centers Stock?”** (13 August 2026) — moderately positive sell-side sentiment despite trailing market performance.

No material M&A, management change, or regulatory enforcement actions appear in the manifest. Strategy appears consistent: grocery-anchored centre ownership, selective acquisition/redevelopment, and dividend growth.
research_rationale: Primary filings confirm improving revenue, NOI, earnings, and covenant-compliant balance-sheet trends that support the screen’s cash-flow and dividend buy case, while truncated MD&A extracts leave REIT-specific operating metrics unverified and leverage plus geographic concentration prevent a stronger conviction overlay.
